introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0595), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: Two hours.**

Answer any FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are NOT allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) With the aid of diagrams, distinguish between serial and parallel data transmission. (5 marks)

(ii) Briefly describe the following modes of transmission giving an example in each case where they are used: Simplex, half duplex, full duplex. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Serial and parallel transmission (5 marks)**

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

- In **serial transmission** the bits of a byte are sent **one after another** (one bit at a time) along a **single** wire or channel. It needs only one wire, so the cable is cheap and the method is reliable over long distances, but it is slower for the same clock speed (used by USB and by networks).
- In **parallel transmission** several bits (for example the 8 bits of a byte) are sent **at the same time**, each on its **own wire**. It is faster over a short distance but needs many wires, which costs more, and the bits can arrive out of step over a long cable (used inside the computer between the CPU and memory, and by old printer cables).

**(ii) Modes of transmission (6 marks, 2 marks each)**

- **Simplex:** data travels in **one direction only**, and the receiver cannot reply. Examples: radio or television broadcasting, keyboard to computer.
- **Half duplex:** data can travel in **both directions, but only one direction at a time**. Example: a walkie-talkie (two-way radio).
- **Full duplex:** data travels in **both directions at the same time**. Example: a telephone or mobile phone call.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Name and briefly explain the functions of the three main parts of the CPU. (6 marks)

(ii) State three main stages of the machine cycle. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three main parts of the CPU (6 marks, 2 marks each: name and function)**

- **Control Unit (CU):** fetches each instruction from memory, decodes it, and sends control signals to the other parts of the computer to make them carry out the instruction in the right order (it coordinates and times all operations).
- **Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU):** carries out the arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and the logical operations and comparisons (AND, OR, NOT, greater than, equal to).
- **Registers:** very small, very fast memory locations inside the CPU that hold the data, the instruction and the addresses that are being processed at that moment.

(Some textbooks give the main memory or the cache memory as the third part; registers are accepted.)

**(ii) Three stages of the machine cycle (3 marks, 1 mark each).** The cycle repeats three stages: **fetch** (the instruction is copied from memory into the CPU), **decode** (the control unit works out what the instruction means) and **execute** (the instruction is carried out). Storing the result is sometimes counted as a fourth stage.
